newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka says rebel attacks show "desperation".
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka says rebel attacks show "desperation".

text.p: A daring attack by separatist Tamil rebels on a flank of advancing Sri Lankan soldiers will not affect the current military thrust into the rebels' northern Wanni stronghold, a senior military official said on Thursday.

Military spokesman Brigadier Sarath Munasinghe said Tuesday's attack by the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) on the military's defence line at Periyamadu, north of the government-held town of Vavuniya, showed the rebels were desperate.
"We see desperation on the part of the LTTE at this juncture," Munasinghe told a news conference in Colombo.
"They have launched two attacks of this nature within a period of two weeks. They are desperate to somehow stop this advance of the army further northwards," he said.
More than 1,000 LTTE rebels attacked the army's artillery and mortar positions near Periyamadu late on Tuesday.
The Defence Ministry said on Wednesday that four officers and 60 soldiers were killed and 68 were wounded in the attack. It said 150 rebels also died and a large number were wounded.

But military officials in the north said on Thursday that 119 soldiers, including four officers, and 182 rebels were killed in the attack, which lasted five hours. Some 190 soldiers were wounded, they added.
An LTTE statement said more than 100 soldiers and 85 rebels were killed.
Anton Rajah, a London-based spokesman for the LTTE, told Reuters the rebels did not attack out of desperation.
"The LTTE is ever more powerful at this stage, in terms of men and women and in equipment and determination. Its ambition is to evict Sinhalese armed forces from the Tamil homeland," Rajah said.
He said the rebels would mount more attacks.
The military launched Operation "Jaya Sikuru", or "Sure of Victory" last month in a bid to open a highway from Vavuniya to the Jaffna peninsula, a further 100 km (60 miles) north.
Vavuniya lies 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo.
Two weeks ago, the rebels mounted a similar attack on the military's rear near Vavuniya, delaying the main offensive.
The LTTE are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east.
The LTTE said in their statement the rebels wiped out the army's entire artillery base at Periyamadu and captured one 120 mm artillery gun and five gun carriages.
But Munasinghe said the six artillery pieces on base had not been touched by the rebels.
Independent confirmation of events is not possible as international media are not allowed in the battle zone.
Official figures show that more than 300 government soldiers have been killed in the offensive since it was launched on May 13. The number of wounded is even higher.
Several hundred LTTE rebels are also reported to have been killed and wounded.
Munasinghe said troops had anticipated the attacks.

"In a way it is far better for us to confront them like this. In any case, in our onward march, these are the people who would be fighting us. So let them come closer and get killed in their numbers," he said.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the ethnic war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
